PreToolUse._comment: mt#2865 dispatch-intent write gate. Deliberately STANDALONE, not GUARD_REGISTRY/dispatcher: dispatch-pretooluse.ts is registered only under the 'Bash|mcp__minsky__session_exec' matcher block above — the session_commit/session_edit_file/session_write_file/session_search_replace/session_pr_create/session_pr_edit tool family this guard gates is NOT among the tool names that already spawn the dispatcher process, so migrating would require widening THAT block's matcher (extra dispatcher spawns for every guard already registered there, for zero benefit — none of them match this tool family). A standalone registration is the cheaper correct choice here, mirroring block-subagent-merge-without-grant.ts's precedent for the sibling D5 merge guard. session_pr_merge is deliberately excluded — already D5-covered by block-subagent-merge-without-grant.ts above. Timeout=30 (PR #2033 R1 NON-BLOCKING #4): matched to parallel-work-guard.ts's timeout (also 30, below) rather than invented — both are standalone PreToolUse guards reacting to session/dispatch-lifecycle tool calls, a closer shape match than ask-permission-bridge.ts's 60 (that guard does live Ask server verification, a heavier network-bound workload this guard never does — it only reads a local JSON file, plus this PR's new exclusive-create lock retry loop, which itself caps at ~1s well inside 30).

mt#3350 success-criteria injection. Surfaces the bound task's `## Success Criteria` verbatim at PR-creation time, so they are confronted at the moment of shipping rather than recalled from having written them (mem#736 R2; the prose tier for this class — /implement-task §7 item 5 — has a measured 14x recurrence across 13 PRs). Matcher is session_pr_create ALONE, deliberately: the two PreToolUse blocks above that mention the tool are multi-tool matchers that also cover session_commit, and injecting the criteria on every commit would be noise that trains the reader to skip them. Not migrated into the dispatcher/GUARD_REGISTRY for the same reason recorded on the dispatch-intent gate above — session_pr_create is not among the tool names that already spawn the dispatcher. Timeout=20: one `minsky tasks spec get` CLI call (budgeted 15s internally) plus process spawn; matched to the sibling stamp-pr-author-link.ts registration on the same tool rather than invented. Fail-open and silent — no task id, no spec, or no criteria section all exit 0 with no output.

mt#3161 run-state writer — records the in-flight tool call (name + start time) so elapsed time is renderable, which the mt#3130 vocabulary makes mandatory rather than optional. matcher '*' fires on EVERY tool. No statusMessage: this runs on every tool call and a per-call status line would be pure UI noise. Budget: the hook's own forward is capped at 500ms internally; timeout 5 covers process spawn.

hooks._comment: ADR-028 guard-dispatcher Stop entrypoint (mt#2357): the SOLE settings.json entry for every Stop-event guard registered in .minsky/hooks/registry.ts's GUARD_REGISTRY (currently six: turn-end-retro-scan at timeoutMs 10s, plus turn-end-untaken-action-scan (mt#3179), turn-end-unwalked-task-scan (mt#3536), and turn-end-unescalated-incident-scan (mt#3593) at 5s each, plus stop-at-decision-scan (mt#3653) at 8s — its budget covers up to two 2.5s `minsky` CLI status reads — plus knowledge-acquisition-detector (mt#3720) at 10s, which moved here from UserPromptSubmit when it was re-grained to one verdict per session). Do not add new individual Stop hook commands here; register them in GUARD_REGISTRY instead. Timeout=49 (host-cap budget model, hook-files.mdc): the family's worst-case SUM — 10+5+5+5+8+10 = 43s — plus the 6s dispatcher overhead margin the prior 21 (=15+6) encoded. Verified 2026-08-05 by summing the live registry rather than this comment's arithmetic: `GUARD_REGISTRY.filter(g => g.event === 'Stop').reduce((a, g) => a + g.timeoutMs, 0)` returns 43000ms across 6 guards. The pre-mt#3653 value was stale at 21 while the sum was already 25: the mt#3536/mt#3593 additions bumped registry timeouts without this comment's required recompute. Bump this whenever a Stop guard is added or its timeoutMs changes. typecheck-on-stop.ts above stays deliberately standalone (predates the framework; emits its own block decisions on its own 60s budget).

Stop._comment: mt#3161 run-state writer — records the turn going idle. Standalone, not a GUARD_REGISTRY entry (observer, not a guard).

SessionEnd._comment: mt#3161 run-state writer — records a SessionEnd HINT only. Per ADR-017, /exit and /clear do NOT fire SessionEnd, so its absence proves nothing; authoritative end/stall detection is the Phase 2 absence sweep.

PostToolUse._comment: mt#3257 subagent model verification — observer, never blocks. Compares tool_input.model (requested alias) against tool_response.resolvedModel (both measured in the Agent PostToolUse payload, sync AND async-launch modes — mt#3257 probes) and warns via additionalContext on mismatch, so a dropped tier override can't silently produce false provenance again (the mt#3151 pin incident). Degraded payloads log to .minsky/subagent-model-mismatch.jsonl instead of warning. Matcher covers Task, the same tool's older name, to stay aligned with the hook's TARGET_TOOL_NAMES (PR #2388 R1). Timeout 10: the hook spawns one bun process and does at most one local file append — no subprocess, no network, no DB — so 10s is generous headroom over sibling 5s reminders purely for cold-start jitter. Override: MINSKY_SKIP_SUBAGENT_MODEL_CHECK.

hooks._comment: ADR-028 D1 guard-dispatcher Phase 2a+2b+mt#2812+mt#2824+mt#2870+mt#2923+mt#2708 (mt#2652, mt#2687, mt#2812, mt#2824, mt#2870, mt#2923, mt#2708): the SOLE settings.json entry for EVERY UserPromptSubmit guard, all migrated (or, for mt#2812/mt#2824/mt#2870/mt#2923/mt#2708, authored directly) onto .minsky/hooks/dispatch-userpromptsubmit.ts's in-process registry (Phase 2a: substrate-bypass-detector, retrospective-trigger-scanner, pre-narration-detector, causal-premise-detector, code-mechanism-assertion-detector, ask-routing-deferral-detector; Phase 2b: auto-session-title, inject-current-time, inject-git-state, inject-prod-state, inject-dispatch-watchdog, memory-search, skill-staleness-detector, mcp-daemon-staleness-detector; mt#2812: guard-health-escalation-detector; mt#2824: silent-stretch-detector; mt#2870: wall-of-text-detector; mt#2923: build-claim-injection-detector; mt#3601: retrospective-completeness-detector; mt#3125: constructed-identifier-batch-detector; mt#2459: operator-deferral-detector; calibration-review-cadence-detector kept last per registry.ts). Do not add new individual hook commands here; register them in .minsky/hooks/registry.ts's GUARD_REGISTRY instead. Timeout=185 (host-cap budget model, hook-files.mdc "Dispatcher host-cap budget model"): this ONE process now runs all twenty-two UserPromptSubmit guards SEQUENTIALLY, so the host cap must cover the family's worst-case SUM, not one guard's budget. Re-verified 2026-07-24 (mt#2459) by SUMMING the live registry rather than trusting this comment's own arithmetic — `GUARD_REGISTRY.filter(g => g.event === 'UserPromptSubmit').reduce((a, g) => a + g.timeoutMs, 0)` returns 185000ms across 22 guards. That check also caught a pre-existing drift this comment had carried since mt#2708: the prose said "Timeout=165" while its own breakdown computed 175s and the field was already 175 — so the narrative figure, not the field, was stale. Re-verified again 2026-08-05 (mt#3720) by the same SUM check: still 22 guards, still 185000ms — but the MEMBERSHIP changed twice since mt#2459 and this narrative had drifted on both, in offsetting directions. retrospective-completeness-detector 10s (mt#3601) joined the family, and knowledge-acquisition-detector 10s (mt#2708) LEFT it for the Stop dispatcher (mt#3720). The field stayed right at 185 by coincidence, not by tracking, which is exactly the failure mode the SUM check exists to catch — do not read an unchanged number as evidence nothing moved. Current breakdown, additive: 145s computed 2026-07-17 (mt#2870) + build-claim-injection-detector 10s (mt#2923) + constructed-identifier-batch-detector 10s (mt#3125) + operator-deferral-detector 10s (mt#2459) + retrospective-completeness-detector 10s (mt#3601) = 185s. The sibling PreToolUse dispatcher entries stay at timeout=15: that family's registry sum is 15s total (check-guessed-session-path 5s + operator-deferral-ask-surface 10s), and no single matcher selects both.

UserPromptSubmit._comment: mt#3161 conversation run-state writer. MessageDisplay._comment: mt#2565: linkifies bare mt#NNNN / PR #N refs in assistant output as it is displayed; the stored transcript keeps the bare ref. This event fires per BATCH OF COMPLETED LINES while a message streams, synchronously in the display path — far hotter than any other event here — so it deliberately does NOT go through the guard dispatcher (ADR-028 D7(5): keep per-invocation IO out of a hot path) and the hook itself loads no domain code. Timeout=5 is a ceiling, not a budget: the measured per-invocation cost is process startup plus a small state-file read. If a SECOND MessageDisplay consumer ever appears, add a dispatch-messagedisplay.ts entrypoint with a transform-shaped outcome rather than a second command here.
